payloads.description: Initial baseline: valid csrf token and benign email to establish normal response, response body, and subscription confirmation page presence.
Safe probe using same observed CSRF token to detect handling differences and where submitted email surfaces.
Stored XSS probe for subscription display; run only after confirming subscription listing/confirmation endpoint from observation prerequisite.

prerequisites.description: Observed CSRF token value available in HAR; use sRlHA2cQXlSVetz3ApxB4TLvIoiRwTpZ for baseline/probe/exploit requests.
Observation required: after baseline/probe submissions, fetch subscription confirmation/listing pages to locate where submitted email appears and capture baseline content and timing.
prerequisites.custom_logic: Perform GET requests to pages likely to display subscriptions (e.g., confirmation page, account pages). Record status code, response time(ms), and body length. Identify exact URL(s) to validate stored XSS results.

oracle_rules.condition: After submission, fetch identified subscription-related pages; if submitted email appears unencoded or raw HTML (includes '<script>alert(1)</script>'), mark as stored XSS.
If subscription page body length increases by >=30% after submission and contains submitted marker, flag stored content.
If missing/invalid CSRF token requests return different status codes (e.g., 200 vs 403/400), flag CSRF enforcement.
If server returns 500 or includes error details when token reused/manipulated, flag potential handling flaw.

test_cases.notes: Chained flow: baseline -> probe -> observe subscription pages -> if display located, run exploit payload. Do not run exploit without confirming display location via observation. Use cookie-based session if available.

payloads.description: Establish baseline response (status, body, timing) for productId=17.
Probe with adjacent productId to detect access differences and to collect timing baseline for comparison.
Inject quote to probe for NoSQL/SQL parsing errors and error messages (safe probe).
NoSQL-style payload to detect error messages or timing anomalies; send after baseline/probe timing collected.

prerequisites.description: Observation required: collect baseline response times and bodies for productId=17 to compute timing anomaly and error signatures.
prerequisites.custom_logic: Perform initial benign GET to /catalog/product?productId=17 and record status code, response time(ms), and body length.

oracle_rules.condition: Compare status code of each request against baseline (productId=17).
Compute body length delta pct between baseline and each other response; flag if >=40%.
If response status is in [400,500] or body contains database/parse error signatures, mark as triggered.
If probe or exploit request response_time - baseline_response_time >= 2000 ms, flag timing anomaly.

test_cases.notes: Order: baseline -> adjacent ID probe -> injection probes. If timing anomaly or error_signature detected, escalate further NoSQL/SQL payloads in a controlled manner. Do not invent endpoints; operate only on observed /catalog/product.

payloads.description: Baseline for postId=3 to capture normal response.
Probe with another observed postId to detect access differences.
Nonexistent postId to provoke differing responses and identify potential IDOR or information leakage.

oracle_rules.condition: Compare status codes against baseline (postId=3 or 4 depending on baseline chosen).
Flag if response body length change >=40% relative to baseline.

test_cases.notes: Run baseline(s) first to detect inconsistent authorization or IDOR. Consolidated tests for both observed postIds to avoid duplication.
